final_candidates.decision_summary: A441 lies in a linker/helix-capping region of HA2; Val may improve hydrophobic packing while preserving fusion-related flexibility.
A410 is in the HA2 coiled-coil core; substitution to Val should increase van der Waals packing and stabilize the trimer without directly changing receptor or fusion-peptide residues.
M404 is adjacent to the HA2 coiled-coil hydrophobic interface; a conservative Leu substitution may improve core packing and folding stability while likely maintaining cell entry.

stop_reason.detail: Further self-iteration without external evidence is unlikely to improve the Top-3 ranking.

history.rationale: K403 lies in the HA2 central coiled-coil; replacing a charged/polar side chain with isoleucine is predicted to improve hydrophobic packing and thermostability while leaving the fusion peptide and receptor site intact.
K403 is likely a solvent-exposed charged residue in the HA2 central coiled-coil; replacing it with Ile risks losing a stabilizing charge/salt-bridge and introducing exposed hydrophobicity.
A410 is positioned in the HA2 stalk helical bundle; the larger valine side chain may fill a nearby cavity and strengthen buried core packing without altering surface recognition.
Ala to Val in the HA2 coiled-coil core can increase van der Waals packing and likely stabilizes the trimer while preserving fusion machinery.
A441 sits in a helical region of the HA2 stalk; substitution to valine is predicted to improve interior hydrophobic contacts and increase global folding stability.
A441 sits in a linker/helix-capping region of HA2; a conservative Val substitution may improve hydrophobic packing without obvious functional disruption.
G392 is likely in a loop/turn between HA2 stalk elements; alanine substitution should reduce backbone flexibility and unfolded-state entropy with low functional impact.
G392 is near the start of the HA2 coiled-coil; Gly-to-Ala can improve helix propensity, though some uncertainty remains about local backbone requirement.
G500 is predicted to lie in a C-terminal HA2 helix or helix-capping region; G->A may increase local helix propensity and contribute to stalk stabilization.
G500A may reduce backbone flexibility in a C-terminal HA2 helical region, increasing local rigidity without directly modifying receptor or fusion-peptide residues.
M404 is within the HA2 coiled-coil; replacement by leucine may optimize core packing geometry and reduce side-chain entropy in the folded state.
M404 is adjacent to the HA2 coiled-coil hydrophobic interface; Leu is a conservative buried-core substitution that may improve folding stability.
A380 is near the base of the HA2 fusion-adjacent region; a conservative increase in side-chain volume could stabilize local packing, though some fusion-related flexibility risk remains.
A380V may improve hydrophobic packing in the proximal HA2 stalk, but the position is close enough to the fusion machinery that functional preservation is less certain.
G361 lies in the HA2 N-terminal stalk region outside the fusion peptide; G->A may reinforce helical structure, but proximity to fusion machinery lowers confidence.
G361 lies near the HA2 fusion peptide/linker; Gly-to-Ala may impair conformational flexibility required for cell entry.

rejection.reason: G361 lies near the HA2 fusion peptide/linker; Gly-to-Ala may impair conformational flexibility required for cell entry.

history.rationale: A149 is predicted to be buried in the HA1 globular domain core; valine may improve hydrophobic packing without directly altering receptor-binding residues.
A149V could stabilize the HA1 head hydrophobic core, but head-domain substitutions may alter receptor binding or antigenic surface properties, so confidence is reduced.
S283 is predicted to lie on a surface-exposed loop; proline substitution may reduce loop entropy and improve thermostability, though effects on local flexibility are uncertain.
Proline introduction in a HA1 head loop may rigidify a functionally important region and risk altering receptor binding or trimer interface contacts.

rejection.reason: Proline introduction in a HA1 head loop may rigidify a functionally important region and risk altering receptor binding or trimer interface contacts.
